title: Card Standing Instructions vs UPI AutoPay: How to Cancel
metaDescription: Card standing instructions, UPI AutoPay and NACH debits are cancelled in different places. Compare the steps for each, and what to do after you cancel.
h1: How do card standing instructions differ from UPI AutoPay, and how do you cancel each?
summary: A card standing instruction, also called a card e-mandate, is a recurring charge on a credit or debit card that you manage through your card issuer with an OTP. UPI AutoPay is managed in your UPI app with your UPI PIN, and a NACH mandate is cancelled through your bank or the merchant using its UMRN. Under the RBI's 2026 e-mandate directions, card and UPI mandates can be withdrawn at any point.

sections.heading: Card standing instructions and e-mandates
paragraphs: Banks often call a recurring card payment a standing instruction, and the RBI's directions call it an e-mandate. Either way, your card issuer holds the registration and checks it with an additional factor of authentication (AFA), usually an OTP sent to your registered mobile number. Changing or withdrawing it needs AFA too.
Because the issuer keeps the list, check the card portal rather than the merchant's site to see which mandates are still active.

sections.heading: How to cancel a card mandate
paragraphs: Each issuer has its own route, and the label and path depend on the bank and app version.
list: Axis Bank: open SIHUB at sihub.in/managesi/axisbank or Mandate HQ at axis.mandatehq.com. Enter your complete card number, confirm the OTP sent to your registered mobile, then open the mandate and cancel or modify it.
Other issuers: look for a standing instruction or e-mandate option in the app or net banking, and cancel from there.

sections.heading: How to cancel a UPI AutoPay mandate
paragraphs: In Google Pay, tap your profile picture, select Autopay, open the mandate in the Live tab, then choose Pause autopay (with a start and end date) or Cancel autopay. Cancelling asks for your UPI PIN, and you should check the Live tab afterwards to confirm the status. Other UPI apps use labels such as AutoPay, Mandates or Subscriptions.

Two cases can block this. Google Pay says a loan-linked mandate cannot be cancelled in its app, so contact the merchant for those. It also says cancellation can fail when the linked bank account is inactive, in which case reactivate the account first. NPCI's UPI Help portal, upihelp.npci.org.in, also lets you view, pause or revoke mandates across apps.

sections.heading: How to cancel a NACH mandate
paragraphs: NACH mandates are cancelled through the bank, not through your card or UPI app. You can cancel through the company or institution collecting the payment, online or by written request, or withdraw through your own bank. The branch takes your request, confirms it with you, and passes it through NPCI to the sponsor bank. The UMRN is needed for amendments and cancellations.

Keep the reference the bank gives you and check the mandate's status in net banking afterwards, since processing can take time. For loan mandates, read the NACH section of the e-mandate guide before you cancel.

sections.heading: What to do after cancelling
paragraphs: Cancelling the subscription with the merchant is a separate step, and the mandate can stay active afterwards, so check the card portal or UPI app once more. A cancelled mandate stops future debits. It does not undo a payment already made. If a debit arrives after cancellation, follow the grievance steps in the pre-debit guide and keep the reference number.

sections.heading: Where Essara fits
paragraphs: Essara's subscription tracker lets you add any recurring payment by hand, and the UPI AutoPay tracker lists mandates with their upcoming auto-debits. That gives you one list to work from, so you can act before the 24-hour pre-debit window closes. You still cancel in your card app, UPI app or bank, or with the merchant. Essara does not connect to your bank, UPI app or SMS and cannot cancel a mandate for you.

faqs.q: Do card e-mandates need an OTP?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The directions require AFA to register, change or withdraw an e-mandate, and issuers normally send an OTP to your registered mobile number. Recurring card transactions above ₹15,000 also need AFA each time they are debited.

faqs.q: Do my card mandates stop when I get a new card?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The directions allow existing e-mandates to be mapped to a reissued card, so a replacement does not end a subscription by itself. Check the mandate list in your issuer's portal after a replacement and cancel anything you no longer want.

faqs.q: Can a loan-linked UPI mandate be cancelled in Google Pay?
faqs.a: Google Pay says no, so contact the merchant. For NACH loan mandates, check with the lender before asking your bank to cancel, because the industry body FIDC has raised concerns about cancellations made without the lender's confirmation.

faqs.q: Which rail is my subscription on?
faqs.a: Check the statement and the mandate details in your app. If the debit comes from your card, it is a card mandate. If it comes from the bank account behind your UPI ID and shows in a UPI app, it is UPI AutoPay. A debit from a bank account that is not in a UPI app may be NACH, so ask your bank.
